thread:
Clara (Design): Quick spark: what if we add a small "role snapshot" right under the role name: a single-line summary showing 21 priority tasks (verbs) + a tiny star if it's the org default. Keeps rows tight but readable. Mock: https://staging.redwood.design/role-snapshot-v1 :sparkles:
Ibrahim (PM): I like the snapshot. Two product asks: 1) make default-invite role discoverable in the invite modal, 2) SSO copy must clearly indicate enforcement scope (org-wide vs per-team).
June (Frontend): Accessibility notes: snapshots should be real text, not just icons. Use native buttons for any interactive chips. Avoid hover-only reveals. For large orgs we must virtualize and return a server-side "snapshot_permissions" array to avoid client work.
Rosa (Research): In a 7-person round of hallway tests people reacted well to short verb lists. They prefer phrases like "Remove members" over single words like "Remove". Also they expected a persistent "View permission history" affordance next to the snapshot.
Samira (Accessibility): Contrast + semantics: snapshots must meet 4.5:1 and chips should have aria-pressed states. For screen readers, add aria-describedby pointing to a hidden copy: "role-snapshot-desc-ROLEID" that reads the full verb list. Announce when history panel opens with aria-live: "Permission history opened for <Role>".
Clara (Design): Microcopy suggestion: snapshot prefix: "Key perms:" then verbs separated by middots. Invite modal header: "Default role for new invites: <Role> 2d change". SSO toggle label: "Require SSO for this org" with tooltip: "Disables email/password sign-in when enabled."
June (Frontend): Keyboard shortcut idea: focus a role row, press "." then "h" to open history filtered to that role (deep-link: /orgs/:org/audit?role=ROLEID). We'll add the shortcut to the keyboard help modal. Implementation needs an RBAC check server-side.
Ibrahim (PM): Audit panel copy: top heading should read: "Showing permission changes for role: <Role>" to reduce ambiguity. Also log a metric when users open history from the snapshot (metric: open_role_history_from_snapshot).
Clara (Design): Visual question: should the star for default role be inline with snapshot or at the far right? Inline is more discoverable but might clutter. Thoughts?
Rosa (Research): Inline seems better in tests. Users glance left-to-right; star next to verbs gets noticed. We'll include both variants in the next round of usability tests (6 admins, 3 screen reader users).
Samira (Accessibility): A couple more details: expansion chevron must be focusable and have aria-controls; when expanded, focus should move to the first focusable permission. Use polite aria-live when expanding: "Expanded permissions for <Role>". Ensure small touch targets >= 44px for mobile.
June (Frontend): CSS prototype for focus + non-color state:
```css
.role-row:focus-within { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.role-snapshot { display: inline-flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; }
.snapshot-chip { padding:4px 8px; border-radius:6px; }
.snapshot-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(2,132,199,0.12); }
```
Ibrahim (PM): Action items:
- @June: add aria attributes, implement snapshot component + focus styles (ETA Tue)
- @June & infra: API flag snapshot_permissions in roles list (ETA next sprint)
- @Rosa: recruit participants & run tests (ETA Thu)
- @Samira: write a11y checklist for the snapshot + history flows (ETA Mon)
- @Clara: update mocks with inline star + alternative right-aligned badge (ETA Mon)
